faqLeft.q: What engine does the Land Rover Range Rover Evoque D150 use?
faqLeft.a: The Evoque D150 uses the Ingenium AJ150D or AJ200D — a 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel. Both are part of the same Ingenium diesel family and share the same rebuild approach. Send us your registration and we'll confirm which one your car has.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Land Rover Range Rover Evoque D150 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £2,200, for either engine code. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my Evoque D150?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm whether you have the AJ150D or AJ200D before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild Ingenium AJ150D Evoque D150 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We replace timing chains, injector seals, EGR components, and gaskets as standard on every AJ150D rebuild.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild Ingenium AJ200D Evoque D150 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The AJ200D is the same engine family as the AJ150D, and we service it to the same standard, replacing timing chains, injector seals, EGR components, and gaskets.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Range Rover Evoque D150 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Evoque D150 if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an Evoque D150 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most Evoque D150 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
